messages:
Maya R: FYI ran a quick canary of spec-decode on ozma-13b-q4f and seeing ~2.6x token/sec but a weird BLEU/QA drop on our multilingual eval set. anyone else seeing this?
Sam B: saw similar on last night run, but thought it was noise from sampling. what's the delta vs non-speculative baseline?
Maya R: baseline (sync decode) BLEU=32.1, spec decode BLEU=28.4. latency and cost look great, but that's a meaningful quality regression.
Priya K: can you paste the exact CLI you used? esp. temperature, top_k, and the spec fallback thresholds.
Maya R: sure — command: `./run_eval --model ozma-13b-q4f --decode speculative --spec.probe_thresh 0.6 --spec.late_bind true --temp 0.8 --top_k 50 --seed 42 --dataset multilingual_eval_v2`
James H: two quick checks: (1) run same seed with `--decode sync` to confirm it's deterministic baseline, (2) run spec with `--spec.probe_thresh 0.9` (more conservative) to see if regression reduces.
Lina T: also validate kv-cache alignment when late_bind is enabled. we've had off-by-one token shifts when cache warming overlaps with speculative fetch.
Maya R: good point — logs show a few `kv mismatch` WARNs. attaching snippet: ```WARN kv_cache: expected 128 entries, got 127 at step 34```
Priya K: that kv warning is suspicious. if speculative path is returning tokens that don't match the main path, eval metrics will diverge even if recovered later. can you dump a small case where outputs differ?
Maya R: putting a small diff in the run artifacts: https://console.redwood/runs/1739123456/diffs — sample id 482 shows divergence after the first sentence.
Sam B: I can repro locally. hypothesis: q4f dequant path + speculative early accept combined causes rounding noise that changes argmax at token boundary. try running with `--quant.stable_rounding true` if available.
James H: also try disabling temperature (set to 0.0) to remove sampling noise and see whether greedy outputs still diverge. that isolates rounding vs sampling.
Maya R: plan: 1) run sync greedy (temp=0) 2) run spec greedy (temp=0) 3) run spec with higher probe_thresh 0.92 4) run spec with quant.stable_rounding true. will post quick numbers in ~15m.
OpsBot: deploy-canary: started canary cluster redwood-dedicated-ozma-13b-q4f-ck1 at 1739123470. will auto-cancel if error_rate > 1.5% in 10m.
Priya K: if kv mismatch persists, we should add an assert in the early-accept path to compare top-3 token logits between spec and main path during debug runs — cheap and catches unstable ties.
Lina T: agree. also log the quantized weight scales for the head layer for the few offending tokens — sometimes a scale mismatch between calibration runs causes instability.
Maya R: update: quick runs done — sync greedy BLEU=31.9, spec greedy BLEU=31.8 (ok), spec temp=0.8 BLEU=28.6 (still low). enabling stable_rounding recovered spec temp=0.8 BLEU=30.9. so quant rounding looks like the main culprit.
Sam B: nice find. does stable_rounding affect latency/cost much?
Maya R: ~+3% latency on microbench, still ~2.5x throughput vs sync. cost tradeoff looks worth it.
James H: next steps: 1) add stable_rounding as default for q4f in canary tier, 2) add kv mismatch telemetry and assertion in debug builds, 3) run a 24h multilingual holdout with stable_rounding on.
Priya K: I'll file a short RFC for changing default quant path with perf numbers and regression tests.
Lina T: I'll add the top-3 logits compare hook to debug runner.
Maya R: thanks team — closing the quick triage, will post RFC link + canary results when ready. :thumbsup:
__notes: thread about speculative decoding + quantization triage; short, realistic Slack style messages; includes code and links
